correctness.rationale: The weighted Matrix-Tree theorem gives the exact rooted-forest partition polynomial including the empty case. Double component selection gives the exact mixed moment and ratio, with zero mixed moment when component sizes do not fit. Strict reciprocal convexity proves fugacity monotonicity and strict Cayley-weight log-convexity establishes the positive low-fugacity boundary, yielding a unique sign transition. A gamma/trigamma crossed-difference calculation proves the fixed-size universal sqrt(3/2) scaling. Exact Prüfer enumeration gives 15 full cases and 180 equality checks; finite checks only corroborate the proof.

originality.rationale: Claim-level comparison distinguishes classical Cayley rooted-forest enumerations, established fugacity measures and root-set determinant formulas, and a newer one-component local law from the explicit pair of distinct component-size counts. Neither the all-pair one-crossing sign theorem nor the common square-root constant appears in the examined full-text primary articles. An inaccessible older report body and generic factorial-moment machinery are documented priority risks; absence from search results is not by itself a novelty proof.
residual_risks: The full body of Pitman Technical Report 457 was not inspected; a relevant multivariate enumeration could imply some finite-moment identities.
General conditioned-assembly generating functions or unpublished work can imply finite-size joint moments. Full priority review by an independent expert remains necessary.

value.rationale: Different component-size counts are natural interacting cluster-population observables in rooted random forests. The theorem classifies all feasible and impossible pairs for all fugacities, proves a unique positivity-to-negativity reversal, and identifies a universal nontrivial square-root limit independent of both sizes. This motivates analysis of cluster-size correlations beyond one-point statistics and is not a routine single numerical instance.
